1.
The present petition has been filed by the petitioners seeking compensation of Rs.
Five Crore Only)
from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its

realization being legal representatives of deceased Sh. Bhupender Singh (married, aged 50 years) on
account of death of deceased who died in road traffic accident in question which occurred on
11.08.2020 at about 1:00 Pm at G.T.K. Road, Tikri Bus Stand towards Delhi

. The petitioners also
prayed for compensation for irreparable monetary loss, mental agony, loss of love and affection and
future prospects plus all other heads of compensation as per entitlement, caused due to accidental
death of deceased.

Macp No. 145/21; Fir No. 386/20; Ps. Alipur Dod: 06.12.2025
2.

The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on
11.08.2020, deceased Bhupender Singh was driving his Tata Ace bearing registration no.
Dl1Lk-4573.

At about 1:00 pm, when he reached at Village Tikri Bus Stand, Gtk Highway Road, a
truck bearing registration no. Rj11-Gb-4303 which was being driven by its driver at a very high
speed, in a rash and negligent manner moving ahead of the vehicle of deceased, suddenly applied
brakes, due to which vehicle of deceased rammed against the aforesaid truck from behind,

as a
result of which deceased sustained grievous injuries

. Thereafter, deceased was taken to Max
Hospital, where he was medically examined and thereafter on 14.08.2020, he succumbed to the
injuries sustained by him in the accident.

Postmortem on the body of deceased was conducted at
Bjrm Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi.

A case U/s 279/337 Ipc was registered at Ps. Alipur vide Fir
No. 386/2020 with regard to the accident in question.

The petitioners have claimed that the
accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned truck which was
allegedly being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner.

The offending vehicle was found

3. The respondent no.1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner have failed to file their Ws despite grant
of sufficient time and opportunities.

Accordingly, their defence was struck off vide order dated
14.12.2021.

Subsequently, they have also stopped appearing Macp No. 145/21; Fir No. 386/20; Ps.

order dated 03.06.2023.
4.

In its written statement, the respondent no. 3 i.e. insurance company raised preliminary
objections that alleged accident was caused on 11.08.2020 and Fir was registered on the next day
and in the said Fir, no offending vehicle was mentioned.

It is claimed that suddenly on 11.11.2020,
the alleged offending vehicle bearing no. Rj11-Gb-4303 was found by one person namely Sh. Hans
Raj who was shown as alleged eyewitness.

It is further claimed that one Sh. Nirmal, nephew of
deceased took the deceased to the hospital after the accident but he did not di

sclose the number of alleged offending vehicle to the police despite the fact that as per the statement of aforesaid alleged eyewitness Sh. Hans Raj, told the number of alleged offending vehicle to the relative of deceased.

It is further claimed that as alleged by the petitioners that nephew of deceased tried to stop the alleged offending vehicle, he remained silent about the registration number of offending vehicle which shows foul play by the petitioners, driver, owner and IO in planting the alleged offending vehicle in the present case.

It is further claimed that IO had served notice u/s. 133 M.V. Act upon the owner of deceased twice and in replies thereto, in first notice, owner had mentioned the date of driving of alleged offending vehicle by its driver Phool Singh as 12.08.2020, however in the second notice,
owner had mentioned the dated 24.08.2020, meaning thereby no one had disclosed to the IO that who was driving the aforesaid vehicle on 11.08.2020 and how IO reached to the conclusion that Phool Singh was driving the vehicle on 11.08.2020 is MACP No. 145/21; FIR No. 386/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 06.12.2025 not explained in the entire DAR.

It is therefore claimed that IO in collusion with the petitioners, driver and owner had planted the alleged offending vehicle as well as driver so that compensation can be taken by the petitioners from the insurance company.
On merits, it has denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

5. From the pleadings of the parties and the documents, following issues were framed vide order dated 14.12.2021:-
1) Whether the eyewitness in the present case has been planted by the petitioners in connivance with the police officials?

6. To substantiate their claim, petitioners have examined six witnesses i.e. PW-1 Sh. Viney (from the office of income tax department), PW-2 ASI Shridhar(first IO), PW-3 Smt. Lalita(widow of MACP No. 145/21; FIR No. 386/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 06.12.2025 deceased), PW-4 Sh. Hansraj (alleged eyewitness), PW-5 SI Dhruv Raj who apprehended the offending vehicle on 11.11.2020 and PW-6 ASI Surender Malik (second IO) and closed their evidence on 22.10.2022.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by respondents no. 1 & 2.

Insurance company/R3 has examined three witnesses i.e. R3W1 ASI Rajinder Singh(who accompanied the IO on 11.08.2020), R3W2 Sh.
Sanjeev Kumar Bhardwaj and R3W3 Sh. Satish Kumar Pruthi and its evidence was closed vide order dated 20.07.2024.

7. I have heard arguments advanced at Bar by learned counsel for the L.Rs of deceased/petitioners and learned counsel for insurance company and have gone through the documents filed alongwith the present claim petition.
ISSUE NO. 1 & 2 8.
The issues no. 1 & 2 are decided together as they require joint consideration.

9. In order to prove the negligence of driver of offending vehicle, the petitioners have examined Sh.
Hansraj, the alleged eyewitness of the accident as PW-4 and Smt. Lalita (widow of deceased) as PW-3.
PW4 deposed that on 11.08.2020 at about 1.00 PM, he was going to Khampur Mandi and when he crossed Tikri Bus Stand, he stopped for filling of air in his vehicle's.
He further deposed that suddenly, he saw a tempo Tata Ace bearing registration no. DL1LK-4573 met with an accident with one truck bearing registration no. RJ11-GB-4303.

He further deposed that the said truck was being MACP No. 145/21; FIR No. 386/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 06.12.2025 driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and driver of the same suddenly applied the brakes, due to which the aforesaid Tata Ace tempo struck against the said truck, as a result of which deceased sustained grievous injuries.
He further deposed that after causing the accident, the driver of the truck ran away from the spot with his vehicle.

He further deposed that after the accident, one of the public person took out diary from the vehicle of deceased and called on the number mentioned on the diary and at the same time, one person claiming himself as nephew of deceased parked his scooty at the road side.
He further deposed that nephew of deceased alongwith several other nearby people took the deceased to Max Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi.
He further deposed that after witnessing the accident, he went to Khampur Mandi.

He further deposed that being an eyewitness,
he helped the injured and gave the number of the truck to the nephew of the deceased.

He further deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving on the part of driver of truck Lalita And Others (Lrs Of Bhupender) vs Phool Singh And Others on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50864963/
4 bearing no. RJ11-GB-4303 and FIR No. 386/2020 has been registered at PS. Alipur.
10.
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that the affidavit in evidence was prepared by the counsel for the petitioner on his instructions.
He further deposed that he did not remember the date of preparation thereof.
He further deposed that the aforesaid affidavit was signed by him at his residence after the same was brought in prepared form by police.
He further deposed that he did not remember whether the contents thereof were read over to him before he had affixed his signatures thereupon.

He MACP No. 145/21; FIR No. 386/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 06.12.2025 denied the suggestion that he did not know the contents of his affidavit or that the same has been filed to get the benefit of compensation to the petitioners in connivance with police.
He further deposed that he himself did not inform the police about the accident.
He further deposed that he had later on gone to the PS and communicated the entire facts about the accident.
He further deposed that he had gone to PS after 3-4 days of the accident.
He further deposed that he was made to go off from PS without obtaining his statement.
He further deposed that he did not remember the name of police personnel as he was shunted out from outside the PS itself.
He volunteered that because of covid pandemic.
He further deposed that he did not make a call at 100 number after he was not permitted to make his statement.
He further deposed that he even did not approach the higher police officials in this regard.
He deposed that he did not send any information with regard to accident through a letter or mail to the police.
He volunteered that later on police officials had come at his residence to make enquiry from him.
He further deposed that he did not remember the date and name of policeman.
He further deposed that they had come after about 15 days of the accident.
He further deposed that his statement was recorded thereafter.
He further deposed that he had not communicated his name, address and phone number to anybody present at the spot after the accident.
He further deposed that he had not communicated his name, address and phone number or any other details to any policeman at PS.
He further deposed that he had not gone to the hospital to meet deceased.
He volunteered that deceased had expired at the spot itself.
He deposed that he did not know as to how the police officials came to know his name and address.

Claims Tribunal is under MACP No. 145/21; FIR No. 386/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 06.12.2025 an obligation to ascertain independently on the basis of material and the evidence which has been brought on record during the course of enquiry as to whose negligence, the motor vehicular accident took place.

11. PW-3 Smt. Lalita has deposed in her evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW3/A that on 11.08.2020 at about 1:00 pm, her husband Sh. Bhupender Singh was driving a tempo Tata Ace bearing registration no. DL1LK-4573 and he was going to deliver spices at Khampur and suddenly driver of one truck bearing registration no. RJ11-GB-4303 which was being driven by him in a very rash and negligent manner applied brakes in the middle of the road nearby Tikri Bus Stand, due to which the aforesaid tempo collided with the truck, as a result of which Sh. Bhupender Singh sustained grievous injuries.
She further deposed that the driver of the truck ran away from the spot.

She further deposed that after the accident, her nephew Nirmal Dixit who was also present at the spot of the accident called her and other known people from the family and took her husband to Max Hospital,
Shalimar Bagh.

During her cross-examination by counsel for insurance company, she deposed that she was not an eyewitness of the accident in question.
13. It is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 386/2020 u/s 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Alipur with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR), would show that same was registered on 12.08.2020 on the basis of DD Entry 0054A recorded with regard to accident call received at PS. Alipur on 11.08.2020 at about 17:09:15 hrs.
As per the said DD No.0054A, the information was given of the accident as well as injured at G.T.K. Road, Tikri Bus Stand.

It may be noted here that no details of the offending vehicle was provided in the aforesaid DD 0054A.
14.

Further, as per the chargesheet the vehicle was seized on 11.11.2020 on DD No.43, as per which,
the caller stated that the vehicle/truck which caused the accident of his father two days back, is MACP No. 145/21; FIR No. 386/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 06.12.2025 standing at the place from where the call was made near Vegetable market.
Upon reaching the spot, as per the statement of PW-5 ASI Dhruv alongwith IO ASI Surender Malik, they met Rajmal and Mohit(son of deceased).

They both stated that they got the information from some acquaintance that the vehicle which caused the accident was at Azadpur Mandi after which they reached the spot and made the call at 100 number.
They also told that on the date of accident, when they made enquries at the spot, one person namely Hansraj told them about the details of the offending vehicle and its registration number.
15. The petitioner has examined PW-4 Sh. Hansraj who is alleged eyewitness.
He has admitted in his cross-examination by the insurance company that he had not communicated his name, address and phone number to anybody present at the spot after the accident.
He further deposed that he had not communicated his name, address and phone number or any other details to any policeman at PS.

It Lalita And Others (Lrs Of Bhupender) vs Phool Singh And Others on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50864963/
6 is very strange that how police officials came to know about the whereabouts of aforesaid witness after about 3 months of the accident and how they went to his house for recording of his statement once he did not disclose his details to anyone including the petitioners and was not even found at the spot when the police officials reached there.

sentences.text: It is further relevant that as per the testimony of PW4, he had told the registration number of the offending vehicle on the date of accident to the nephew of deceased.
Despite that no call regarding the same was made to the police mentioning the registration number of the offending vehicle on the date of accident.

She also failed to inform the same to the police on the date of accident as the details of the alleged offending vehicle came to be known only on 11.11.2020.
16.

During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioners argued that the registration number could not be told to the police due to covid pandemic and as per testimony of PW-4, he was not entertained by the police officials when he had gone to the PS.
It is therefore argued that due to said reason, the details of the offending vehicle could not be told to the police.

Even if the said contentions are considered, it is questionable as to why petitioners failed to disclose the registration number of alleged offending vehicle to the police when the dead body of deceased was handed over to his relative on 14.08.2020 i.e., when they came into contact of police officials.

Accordingly, the petitioners have failed to explain the delay of about 3 months in providing the registration number of offending vehicle to the police during investigation despite saying that they had knowledge of registration number of the offending vehicle since the date of accident.

Hence, the presence of eyewitness at the spot become doubtful and the case of the petitioners seems improbable as instead of disclosing the details of the offending vehicle to the police officials, they themselves reached the spot where the alleged offending vehicle was parked after about 3 months of the accident.

17. Further, the testimony of PW-6/IO who had seized the alleged offending vehicle stated in his cross-examination that he came to know about the name of the driver of the offending vehicle on MACP No. 145/21; FIR No. 386/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 06.12.2025 11.11.2020 at the instance of the registered owner when he gave her notice u/s. 133 M.V. Act.

As per record, the respondent no. 2 registered owner of alleged offending vehicle in her replies to the notices u/s. 133 M.V. Act given to her by the IO had mentioned the dates as 12.08.2020 and 24.08.2020, however the date of accident in the present case is 11.08.2020.
Therefore, it is also not clear as to who was driving the alleged offending vehicle on the date of accident.
18. It is apparent from the statement of PW-2 ASI Shridhar that he enquired at the spot, however, he was not able to find any eyewitness of the accident in question.

He further deposed that till the time,
he was the IO, no one had approached to give any information about the accused and about the involvement of particular vehicle in the accident in question.

During his cross-examination, he admitted that after his thorough investigation at the spot, after the accident, he was not able to find or get any clue in respect of any eyewitness, the vehicle involved in the accident as well as driver till 01.10.2020, the day he was transferred.
Hence, this shows that neither any eyewitness nor the details of the offending vehicle were known till 01.10.2020.

sentences.text:
In view of the above, petitioners have failed to bring on record any evidence to show that the accident was caused by alleged offending vehicle i.e., Truck bearing registration no. RJ11-GB-4303.
20.

Hence, in view of above discussion it is held that the petitioners have failed to prove even on the principles of preponderance of probabilities the involvement of offending vechicle MACP No.
145/21; FIR No. 386/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 06.12.2025 bearing registration no. RJ11-GB-4303 in the present case.

Therefore, petitioners have failed to prove that the deceased Sh. Bhupender Singh,
suffered fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 10.04.2015 near Kali Mandir, GTK Road,
Azadpur Mandi, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of truck bearing registration no.
RJ11-GB-4303 by respondent no. 1.
Issue no.1 & 2 are accordingly decided in favour of respondents and against the petitioners.
ISSUE NO.3 21.
In view of findings on issue no.1 & 2(supra), it is clear that the petitioners have failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of truck bearing no. RJ11-GB-4303.

Since, this is a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the petitioners have failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities,
hence they are not entitled to any compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
22.
In view of findings on issues no. 1 to 3 (supra), present claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is dismissed.
Copy be given dasti.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.

3 GB-4303, owned by Shabnam Khan/R-2 and insured with M/s.
ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd./R-3?
OPP. 
3) Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?OPP.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even if the said contentions are considered, it is questionable as to why petitioners failed to disclose the registration number of alleged offending vehicle to the police when the dead body of deceased was handed over to his relative on 14.08.2020 i.e., when they came into contact of police officials.
Accordingly, the petitioners have failed to explain the delay of about 3 months in providing the registration number of offending vehicle to the police during investigation despite saying that they had knowledge of registration number of the offending vehicle since the date of accident.
Hence, the presence of eyewitness at the spot become doubtful and the case of the petitioners seems improbable as instead of disclosing the details of the offending vehicle to the police officials, they themselves reached the spot where the alleged offending vehicle was parked after about 3 months of the accident.
As per record, the respondent no. 2 registered owner of alleged offending vehicle in her replies to the notices u/s. 133 M.V. Act given to her by the IO had mentioned the dates as 12.08.2020 and 24.08.2020, however the date of accident in the present case is 11.08.2020.
Therefore, it is also not clear as to who was driving the alleged offending vehicle on the date of accident.
Hence, this shows that neither any eyewitness nor the details of the offending vehicle were known till 01.10.2020.
In view of the above, petitioners have failed to bring on record any evidence to show that the accident was caused by alleged offending vehicle i.e., Truck bearing registration no. RJ11-GB-4303.
20.
Therefore, petitioners have failed to prove that the deceased Sh. Bhupender Singh,
suffered fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 10.04.2015 near Kali Mandir, GTK Road,
Azadpur Mandi, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of truck bearing registration no.
RJ11-GB-4303 by respondent no. 1.
In view of findings on issue no.1 & 2(supra), it is clear that the petitioners have failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of truck bearing no. RJ11-GB-4303.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Issue no.1 & 2 are accordingly decided in favour of respondents and against the petitioners.
ISSUE NO.3 21.
Since, this is a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the petitioners have failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities,
hence they are not entitled to any compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
22.
In view of findings on issues no. 1 to 3 (supra), present claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is dismissed.
Copy be given dasti.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
